Method of Attack: Traffic direction system (TDS) used to redirect potential victims matching specific profiles to phishing and malware-dropping sites
Distribution of remote access trojans (RATs) via fake browser update notices
Use of malicious web shells and PHP backdoor scripts to extract client information and forward requests to command and control (C2) servers
Phishing Microsoft credentials via fake login pages
Impacted Systems: Servers hosting 16,500 websites including universities, local governments, adult content platforms, personal blogs
Poorly secured CMS sites such as WordPress
Users in Brazil, India, United States, Singapore, Indonesia
Attack Vector: Compromised web servers with malicious JavaScript and PHP backdoors
Indicators of Compromise: Malicious web shells on compromised servers
PHP backdoor scripts forwarding to Parrot TDS C2 servers
Payload-dropping URLs with fine-tuned user profiling
